h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When edge 2 is already a 3x3 the parent tends to sit near the conv-rich accuracy ceiling, so completing the 0->1->2->3 conv chain yields smaller marginal gains.
A 0->3 identity turns the 0->1->3 conv path into a residual branch, which in NAS-Bench-201 is the pattern of top cells, so the conv trains easily and adds more.
A 0->3 residual shortcut stabilizes optimization so added conv depth on 0->2 feeding the output is more usable.
Node 1 built by a 1x1 lacks spatial aggregation, so a 3x3 on 1->3 supplies a missing capability rather than duplicating one.
Node 1 already holds 3x3 features, so another serial 3x3 on 1->2 gives diminishing returns in an already strong parent.
When 2->3 already delivers conv features to the output, a pooled 1->3 branch is diluted rather than dominant, so the usual pooling penalty is smaller.
If 1->2 already carries conv features, a pooled input branch only adds a low-pass component to node 2 and is less damaging.
When node 2 receives blurred input via a pool, a conv on 2->3 converts it into discriminative features instead of passing low-information content to the output.
An input->output identity is most valuable as the residual partner of a conv output branch, matching the skip-plus-conv structure of top NAS-Bench-201 cells.
A skip on 1->3 forwards node 1 directly to the output and is worth more when node 1 holds learned 3x3 features rather than raw or pooled input.
